correctness.rationale: The size-k matching count of the 2n-boundary cycle and conditional uniform matching deletion give the polynomial identity for all valid n,k. Simple chords cross nothing, so exact crossing preservation is justified. The finite transform follows by binomial factorial expansion and coefficient extraction. The Poisson–Gaussian joint characteristic function follows from an a_{n,k}<=2 dominated-summand bound and the established crossing marginal central limit theorem; no independence is inferred from correlation alone. A standalone verifier passed 487 direct exact checks, including all matchings for n<=7.

originality.rationale: The proposed contribution is the complete bivariate simple-chord/crossing transfer and resultant joint asymptotic independence. Acan (2015), Flajolet–Noy (2000), and Paguyo (2021) establish the respective separate marginals, while earlier work already contains the finite covariance (excluded here). The inspected primary sources do not directly state or strongly cover the joint transform. Residual risk of an implicit classical bivariate enumerator is acknowledged.

value.rationale: The exact bivariate identity determines all crossing distributions conditional on the natural local simple-chord count, including simple-chord-free diagrams, from known crossing-only enumerators. The joint Poisson/Gaussian independent limit is a meaningful structural decoupling of local and global chord-diagram fluctuations and does not follow from separate convergence or covariance decay. This goes materially beyond recomputing the known covariance.
